title: Quantitative analysis of myofiber type composition in human and mouse skeletal muscles
protocol: Clean all the equipment with 70% alcohol.
Adjust the chamber temperature and the object temperature to −20°C and −22°C, respectively.
Place all the materials required for cutting inside the cryostat chamber to equilibrate to the temperature.
Install the anti-roll glass and a blade inside the cryostat chamber.
Adjust the thickness of cryosections to 16 μm thick for human tissue or 10 μm thick for mouse tissue.
Transport the muscle biopsy in liquid nitrogen to the cryostat.
Leave the biopsy inside the cryostat chamber to equilibrate to the temperature for 15–30 min.
Put Tissue-Tek on the specimen holder and place the muscle biopsy using tweezers.
Place the specimen holder in the cryostat block.
Collect the cryosections onto the SuperFrost slide.
Assess tissue quality by checking the first section under a normal bright-field microscope.
Exclude samples with extensive freezing damage from further analysis.
Examine if there are more cross-sections of myofibers rather than longitudinal sections of myofibers.
Detach muscle biopsy from specimen holder and place it again with correct orientation to get cross-sections if needed.
Collect three cryosections per biopsy onto SuperFrost slides.
Air dry slides stored at -20°C for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Outline each cryosection with an immunopen about 2–3 mm from the tissue edge.
Wash the cryosections in PBST in the staining box.
Proceed with blocking.
Incubate slides in PBST + 5% milk for 30 min.
Wash the slides three consecutive times with a large volume of PBST, each time for 5 min.
Incubate sections with a mixture of rabbit anti-laminin and mouse anti-6H1 detecting MyHC2X for 2 h at room temperature.
Wash the slides three consecutive times with an excessive volume of PBST, each time for 5 min.
Incubate sections with goat anti-rabbit-conjugated-Alexa Fluor® 750 and goat anti-mouse-conjugated-Alexa Fluor® 488 for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the slides three consecutive times with an excessive volume of PBST, each time for 5 min.
Incubate the sections with a mixture of BA-D5-conjugated-Alexa Fluor® 350 detecting MyHC1 and SC-71-conjugated-Alexa Fluor® 594 detecting MyHC2A overnight at 4°C.
Wash the slides three consecutive times with an excessive volume of PBST for 5 min.
Wash the slides once with an excessive volume of PBS for 5 min.
Cover the sections with ProLong™ Gold antifade reagent.
Cover the slide with a cover slip.
Fix the cover slip with nail polish.
Incubate for 24 h at room temperature in the dark.
Store slides at 4°C prior to imaging.
Calculate a shading profile using the ‘Shading Reference From Tile Image’ in ZEN Lite for each channel in each slide.
Load all shading profiles for one specific channel into Fiji and combine them into a stack using the ‘Images to Stack’ command.
Use ‘Z Project’ with ‘Projection type’ set to ‘Median’ to calculate the median shading profile for this channel.
Repeat steps b-c for all channels.
Use the median shading profiles for the shading correction using
Check and correct the generated masks.
Remove artifacts such as tissue folds, out-of-focus regions, scratches, and dirt objects.
Open Fiji.
Select Freehand Selection Tool.
Run “1.Tiff_to_Mask.ijm” macro to generate a mask for each image.
Provide a directory with merged tiff images.
For the first image that pops up, check if the generated mask is accurate.
Press OK button if the generated mask is correct.
Adjust the mask if necessary.
Zoom in or out on the area of interest by holding Ctrl and scrolling the mouse wheel.
Hold Shift and Right Click to add an area to the mask.
Hold Alt and Right Click to remove an area from the mask.
Press OK when finished adjusting the mask.
Open Fiji.
Run “2.Masked_Lamin.ijm” macro to generate a masked copy of laminin for each image.
Provide a directory with “_Mask” tiff images.
For each image, save a tiff file that ends with “_Lamin_Masked” in the input directory provided.
Run Ilastik software.
Create a new “Pixel Classification” project.
Input data.
Click on “1. Input Data” menu on the left.
Add New button to add image(s).
Select multiple images with “_Lamin_Masked” extension that represent your dataset.
Click on “Open” button.
Feature selection.
Select “2. Feature Selection” menu on the left.
Define features by clicking on “Select Features…” button.
Training.
Select “3. Training” menu on the left.
To train the classifier, define labels corresponding to two classes: ‘myofiber boundary’ and ‘not myofiber boundary’.
Zoom in on different areas to annotate the classes.
Select one of the classes.
Open Command Prompt.
Run the command below by providing paths required: “[Path to Ilastik]\ilastik.exe” --headless --project="[Path to classifier saved]\3.pixelclass_lamin_masked.ilp” [Path to image]\∗_Lamin_Masked.tif
For each image, a tiff file that ends with “Masked_Probabilities” will be saved in the image directory.
Open Fiji.
Run “4.Segment_Lamin.ijm” macro to segment and generate the ROIs for each image.
Provide a directory with “Masked_Probabilities” tiff images.
For each image, generate a tiff file with “_Segmentation” extension in the input directory.
Save an ROI file ending with “_ROI” in the ROI subdirectory.

Extract mean-fluorescence-intensity and ROI properties using Fiji measurements: “Area”, “Mean gray value”, “Standard deviation”, “Modal gray value”, “Min & max gray value”, “Shape descriptors”, “Median”.
Add an extra channel (channel 5) to show results of the pixel-classification step.
Evaluate segmentation quality using the “Mean gray value” on the border of each ROI.
Open Fiji.
Run “5.Export_MFI_and_Laminin_Int_and_Distance.ijm” macro for the laminin segmentation and generate the regions-of-interest (ROI) (individual myofibers) for each image.
Provide a directory with tiff images.
For each image, save a tab-delimited text file that ends with “_MFI” in the ROI subdirectory.
Save three jpeg images that end with “_check[X]” in the check subdirectory.
Exclude non-myofiber ROIs in image processing based on percentiles of segmentation certainty, CSA, and circularity values.
Verify the thresholds applied by visualizing filtered ROIs using the provided macro.
Filter out longitudinally sectioned myofibers and elongated ROIs using circularity measure.
Draw a density plot of the entire dataset to define a filtering threshold.
Apply filtering for circularity based on the 1st percentile threshold.
Include ROIs with Circularity > 1st percentile.
Visualize filtered ROIs using the “6.Visual_Check_Filtering.ijm” macro available on GitHub.
Save a tab-delimited text file (with “_Filt” extension) in the ROI subdirectory.
Open Fiji.
Run “6.Visual_Check_Filtering.ijm” macro to visualize the filtered ROIs.
Provide directory with tiff images and ROI subdirectory.
For each sample, save a jpeg file that ends with “_check4” in the image directory.
Select one section per sample for further analysis.
Consider only samples with a minimum of one hundred myofibers for downstream analysis.
Cluster the myofibers by running “clustering” R chunk code.
Scale MFI values for each of the three MyHC isoforms per sample without centering using "ScalingAndTransformation" R chunk code.
Implement mean-shift algorithm using LPCM R package to cluster objects based on transformed (natural logarithm) MFI values.
Remove the cluster with a low proportion of myofibers (typically < ∼2%).
Draw boxplots to visualize the myofibers clusters.
Generate a spatial visualization of the clustering assignment per myofiber.
Calculate the proportion of myofibers in each cluster per sample.
